Hi Elaine — thank you for the clear list, and for attaching the PDF.

Quick summary from our side: we absolutely want to avoid protracted redlines. Two things to flag up front: 99.99% uptime is materially higher than our standard 99.95% baseline for hosted plans and would change credit exposure significantly; and the automatic crediting language will need legal and finance alignment.

I've attached a short set of initial redline suggestions (RW_redlines_SLA_20280615.docx) that try to preserve your operational asks while protecting rollout flexibility and reasonable exposure for us. High-level alternatives we propose:
- Offer 99.97% for the production tier on a 12‑month committed plan (trade for a higher minimum monthly committed spend).
- Maintain auto-crediting for availability shortfalls but cap monthly credits at X% of monthly recurring charges (we propose 30%).
- Accept 30-minute P1 response, 4‑hour initial remediation SLA, but keep resolution targets as objectives with escalation paths rather than absolute contractual obligations.
- Agree to a single 4‑hour maintenance window per region per month; require 7-day advanced notice for scheduled maintenance and 14 days only for major disruptive changes.

Ben from Sales Ops and Laura from Legal are cc'd — Laura, could you weigh in with the legal redline posture? If this looks broadly acceptable to BrightLane we can schedule a 30-minute call Monday to finalize trade-offs.

Elaine / Ava — quick operational note from Sales Ops before Legal weighs in.

We ran the ask through our cost model (capacity + commitment delta): moving to 99.99% without a committed spend increase would require us to reserve additional dedicated capacity for your production tier and/or change our routing fallbacks. Estimated uplift to monthly charges for 99.99% is ~+40% compared to our 99.95 baseline.

Given that, our recommended path is the 99.97% compromise on a 12-month commit that Ava proposed — it reduces our capital exposure and gives BrightLane stronger availability guarantees. On auto-crediting: we can accept auto crediting with a cap and an annual aggregate limit (we suggest cap = 30% MRC and annual aggregate = 100% MRC) so we don't create unlimited downside.

I'll note the maintenance request: the single 4-hour window per region per month is workable operationally, but the 14-day advance-for-everything ask is a tight constraint. We should distinguish between routine maintenance (7 days notice) and major upgrades (14 days + rollback plan).

Ava — Laura, pinging you for the formal redlines to share back to BrightLane.

Hi all — I reviewed the requested positions and produced a tracked-changes doc (MSA_OrderForm_redlines_legal_ava.docx). Summary of our recommended contractual posture below (aimed at a single clean compromise that legal will accept without further escalations):

1) Availability target and credits
- Offer: 99.97% monthly availability for the "Production" tier when Customer signs a 12-month minimum order form with a committed spend threshold.
- Credits: Automatic pro rata credits for monthly availability shortfalls, capped at 30% of the monthly recurring charges per month; annual aggregate cap = 100% of MRC. Credits are the sole and exclusive remedy for availability shortfall.

2) Response and resolution
- Response times: P1 — 30 minutes; P2 — 2 hours; P3 — next business day.
- Resolution: we will use target resolution times as internal objectives; contractual commitments will reference response times and escalation cadence. For clarity, we will add an operational runbook attachment that defines SLA handling (incidents, severity definitions, escalation contacts).

3) Maintenance windows and notice
- Agree to one standard maintenance window per region per month (4 hours, scheduled UTC Saturday window).
- Routine maintenance: 7 business days' notice required.
- Major upgrades/changes that may cause downtime: 14 days' notice + rollback plan.
- Emergency maintenance: permitted with notice as soon as practicable; not treated as an availability breach if performed in accordance with the emergency clause.

4) Miscellaneous
- We will include a conditional clause: if Customer requires 99.99% (higher than 99.97%), we will provide that via an addendum with adjusted fees and possibly additional reserved capacity commitments.

Please see the attached tracked-change doc for precise language. Elaine — if BrightLane is willing to accept the 99.97% + commitment path, we can route the revised Order Form to DocuSign and schedule a final sign-off call next week.
